name: Shillong
description: Capital of Meghalaya and headquarters of East Khasi Hills district. Known as the Scotland of the East, it sits at about 1,500 m elevation with pine forests, colonial architecture, markets, and is the main base for exploring the district.
facts: Named after the deity Lei Shyllong

name: Sohra (Cherrapunji)
description: Town in East Khasi Hills famous as one of the wettest places on Earth. Gateway to dramatic waterfalls, living root bridges, caves, and the southern escarpment overlooking Bangladesh plains.
facts: Base for Nohkalikai and living root bridge treks

name: Nohkalikai Falls
description: Tallest plunge waterfall in India, dropping about 340 m (1,115 ft) off the Sohra plateau escarpment into a turquoise pool. Named after a local legend of Ka Likai.
facts: Best in monsoon; green plunge pool below

name: Nohsngithiang Falls (Seven Sisters Falls)
description: Seven-segmented waterfall dropping ~315 m over limestone cliffs near Mawsmai village. Also called Seven Sisters or Mawsmai Falls; dramatic views over Bangladesh plains.
facts: Best during monsoon for full flow

name: Elephant Falls
description: Three-tier waterfall on the outskirts of Shillong, locally Ka Kshaid Lai Pateng Khohsiew. Cascades over fern-covered rocks; easily accessible with steps and viewing points.
facts: Named after an elephant-shaped rock (destroyed in 1897 quake)
Popular short stop on way to Sohra

name: Shillong Peak
description: Highest point in Meghalaya at about 1,966 m, offering panoramic views of Shillong and surrounding hills. Site of reverence for the deity Lei Shyllong; popular for sunsets.

name: Mawlynnong Village
description: Village in Pynursla block known as Asia's cleanest village. Features living root bridges, a balancing rock, and views toward the Bangladesh border; community-managed cleanliness.
facts: Declared cleanest village in Asia (2003) and India
Community tourism and living root bridges

name: Double Decker Living Root Bridge (Nongriat)
description: Iconic two-tier living root bridge in Nongriat village, grown from Ficus elastica roots by Khasi communities over centuries. Reached by a steep trek of thousands of steps from Tyrna.

name: Mawphlang Sacred Forest
description: Ancient sacred grove (Law Lyngdoh) preserved by Khasi tradition near Mawphlang village. Strict rule against removing anything; rich biodiversity and megaliths; guided walks.
facts: Protected by local beliefs for centuries
No collection of plants or wood allowed

name: Mawsmai Cave
description: Accessible limestone show cave near Sohra with lit passages, stalactites, and fossils. Short tourist route suitable for most visitors; one of the first developed caves in the area.
facts: Khasi name means Oath Stone Cave

name: Ward's Lake
description: Man-made horseshoe-shaped lake in central Shillong, built in 1894. Surrounded by botanical gardens, wooden bridge, boating, and popular for walks and relaxation.
facts: Locally Nan Polok or Pollock Lake

name: Laitlum Canyon
description: Dramatic cliff-edge viewpoint overlooking deep valleys and layered hills, about 25 km from Shillong near Smit. Popular for sunrises, sunsets, and panoramic photography.
facts: Name means end of hills in Khasi

name: Kongthong Village (Whistling Village)
description: Village famous for its unique whistling language (Jingrwai Iawbei) where each person has a unique tune as a name. Features living root bridges and community tourism.

name: Don Bosco Centre for Indigenous Cultures
description: Museum in Mawlai, Shillong showcasing the cultures, artefacts, costumes, and lifestyles of indigenous peoples of Northeast India across multiple galleries.
